title: Annotatio IV §.XII: Mejerus — Damascene author of new scholastic method; simple doctrine mutated
pass_a_gloss: He is also guilty of very many other innovations and Terms afterward called scholastic, rashly enough thrust into sacred Religion and Christian Theology — nay, postulated as Author by the often-praised Mejerus, who begins the third paragraph of his eighth Section thus: Moreover in this age there takes head a new way of treating the doctrine of the Christian religion, with Damascene as author, who first instituted to hand it down after the manner of a science. He, omitting certain momentous articles, brought thorny and useless questions into Theology, proposed new opinions of doctors as dogmas of the Christian religion, more rarely appealed to Scripture; neglected the form of sound words, using formulas of philosophers rather than of ancient theologians and of scripture. And because most Doctors who followed afterward embraced that way of treating, gradually the simple manner of the ancients’ doctrine concerning the Christian religion was changed into scholastic disputations (pp. 174 and 175).
pass_b_english: Guilty also of many later ‘scholastic’ terms rashly thrust into sacred theology — Mejerus names Damascene author of a new scientific method of treating Christian doctrine.

Thorny useless questions; new opinions as dogmas; rare appeal to Scripture; philosopher-formulas over sound words — and followers gradually turned the ancients’ simple doctrine into scholastic disputations.
source_text: aliarum quoque plurimarum innovationum & Terminorum, scholasticorum deinceps dictorum, temerè satis sanctæ Religioni & Theologiæ Christianæ intrusorum reus, quin Autor postulatus à sæpius laudato Mejero, paragraphum tertium Sectionis suæ octavæ ita exorso: Capita prætereà hôc seculo nova ratio tractandi doctrinam religionis Christianæ, auctore Damasceno, qui eam, ad modum scientiæ, primus tradere instituit. Hic, omissis quibusdam momentosis articulis, spinosas & inutiles quæstiones in Theologiam intulit, novas doctorum opiniones, ut religionis Christianæ dogmata proposuit, rarius ad Scripturam provocavit; formam sanorum verborum neglexit, formulis philosophorum potiùs, quam theologorum antiquorum & scripturæ utens. Et quia plerique postsecuti Doctores istam tractandi rationem sunt amplexi, sensim simplex veterum de religione Christianâ doctrinæ ratio, mutata est in scholasticas disputationes. p. 174. & 175.
